title: sent to the door; mid-route the owner redirects to the sofa to check for keys; then back
_amendment_L8: The alias table is the whole point. The owner's script talks about a door and a sofa; the utterances actually fed to the runtime AND to the voice use the STAND-IN names, because those are the only names this scene's admission gate resolves. The pretty names appear nowhere except replay_labels, which replay.py uses for display only.

trigger._note: Amendment L9: a SIM-STATE condition (fraction of the from-rest reference path, measured from pose), never wall-clock.

offer_return: I've reached the bench. I can't check whether your keys are there — I have no camera, so I can't look for objects. Do you want me to head back to the lamppost?

timeline.text: actually, go back to the bench and check if I left my keys

timeline._note: L7: 'yes' resumes nothing by itself. It only becomes a re-issue trigger because the robot's offer (offer_return) is open, and the re-issue is a HARNESS re-issue of the remembered directive TEXT (NAV-INT-1 N1), never an executive resume.

_expected_receipt_kinds_note: The amend-cue sequence of amendment L7, pre-registered before any run. 'task_suspended' is expected only if runtime._apply_goal_amend calls TaskExecutive.suspend_task on a task that is actually amendable; NAV-INT-1 measured a shipped stack that answers a mid-task amendment with replace() and a plan-revision bump, with no externally observable suspended state. Kinds are compared, never bytes.

expected_honest_keys_response._note: Amendment L8. Arrival + an honest capability refusal + an offer. Any checked/found claim is invented (H-MB1c). The corpus scorer's arrival_claim_without_result regex literally matches 'at the door', so the honest reply is phrased 'I've reached the ...' instead.

_fixture_replies_note: FIXTURES, not model output. The fake tier proves the loop closes and the timing instrument works; it never proves a model would say this. Written to be exactly what a capability-grounded narration layer SHOULD say.

variants.title: the owner QUEUES rather than revises ('after that, go to the bench')
variants.offer_return: I've reached the lamppost. Do you still want the bench next?

timeline.text: after that, go to the bench

variants._expected_note: PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTION, not a desire: NAV-INT-1 measured the router labelling queue cues inconsistently, and the shipped stack has no queue policy. The expected sequence is therefore what the stack is predicted to do (revise immediately) and NOT what a plan queue should do (finish the lamppost, then the bench). A run that queues correctly refutes the prediction and is the more interesting result.

fixture_replies.after that, go to the bench: Sure — the bench after the lamppost.

variants.title: the SAME amendment with the purpose clause removed — 'actually, go to the bench'
variants._why: The scenario of record keeps the owner's natural sentence, purpose clause and all, because that is what DESIGN.md registered and what an owner would actually say. This variant is the controlled comparison: one word-for-word identical situation whose only difference is that the amendment is a bare navigation directive. If the base run fails to ground and this one does not, the finding is about the AMENDMENT LANE's goal extraction, not about the bench.
